statement: statement: For every arithmetic formula F over a commutative ring with s leaves and binary + and × gates, there is a uniform construction of an algebraic branching program with O(s) edges computing exactly F, without any restriction on repeated variables. Proof: For a leaf labelled by a variable or constant, use a single source-to-sink edge with that label. Inductively, suppose G and H have source-to-sink ABPs with disjoint internal vertices. For F=G+H, take disjoint copies and identify their sources and identify their sinks; the source-to-sink path weights are exactly the paths of either child, so their sum is G+H. For F=GH, take disjoint copies and identify the sink of G with the source of H; every source-to-sink path is uniquely a path in G followed by a path in H, so its weight is the product of their weights, and summing over all such paths gives GH. These constructions preserve the represented polynomial by induction. Each formula node contributes at most a constant number of identifications and the child edge sets are retained, so the resulting number of edges is at most the number of leaves, hence O(s). The construction follows the formula tree and is uniform. This establishes ordinary ABP conversion only; it makes no claim of a common variable order, obliviousness, linearity in placeholder variables, or conversion of arbitrary IPS/NS/PC derivations.

proof: Induct on F's formula tree. A leaf is represented by a one-edge ABP labeled by its variable or constant. At an internal sum or product, the child variable sets are disjoint because F is globally read-once. label: S0090
statement: statement: For every commutative ring R and polynomial F in at most k variables of total degree at most d, F has an equivalent layered oblivious arithmetic branching program of size O(d * binom(d+k,k)), with layers in a fixed variable order and with repeated occurrences allowed. Proof: Write F = sum_alpha c_alpha x_1^alpha_1 ... x_k^alpha_k over exponent vectors alpha with sum alpha_i <= d. There are at most binom(d+k,k) such vectors. For each nonzero monomial, create a source-to-sink path whose edge labels, in the fixed variable order, are alpha_i copies of x_i for each i, with the coefficient c_alpha on one edge; the path weight is that monomial. Put these paths in parallel by merging their sources and sinks, so the path-sum is F. Each path has at most d variable edges plus at most one coefficient edge, hence the size is O(d * binom(d+k,k)) (with the constant and zero-polynomial cases represented directly). The construction is effective from the coefficient list. This proves an ordinary layered oblivious ABP representation for bounded-variable-support polynomials; it does not imply a read-once ABP representation when some exponent alpha_i exceeds one.

label: S0096
statement: statement: Lemma (restricted certificate compilation with explicit size accounting). Let R be a commutative ring and let F(x,z) be an arithmetic formula with s gates, where each variable occurs at most once and F is syntactically linear in z. If F(x,0)=0 and F(x,Q(x))=1 hold as polynomial identities, then a uniform construction produces a layered oblivious ABP computing the same polynomial, with O(s^2) edges; it remains linear in z and satisfies both identities. Proof: Induct on the formula tree. Represent each leaf by a one-edge ABP. At an internal gate, the children have disjoint variable sets by read-once-ness. Concatenate their variable orders and pad missing layers with weight-1 edges. For addition, join the padded child programs in parallel between a common source and sink; the path-sum is the sum of their polynomials. For multiplication, concatenate the programs; the path-sum is their product. Thus each constructed program computes exactly the formula at its root. Exact polynomial equality preserves syntactic z-linearity as a semantic property (degree in z at most one), and preserves both displayed identities by substitution. The construction has at most s layers and at most O(s) copied edges per layer, hence O(s^2) edges and polynomial construction time. This establishes the conversion only when the supplied certificate itself is read-once; it does not imply a conversion for arbitrary IPS certificates.

statement:
statement: Lemma (syntactic occurrence bounds degree). Let R be a nonzero commutative ring and F a syntactic arithmetic formula over R, with constants from R and binary + and × gates. For every variable x, deg_x(F) is at most the number occ_x(F) of x-leaves in F. Thus a formula with at most one x-leaf cannot compute x^2 as a formal polynomial.
proof: Induct on the formula tree. A constant leaf has x-degree 0 and zero x-occurrences; an x-leaf has degree and occurrence count 1; any other variable leaf has degree and occurrence count 0. At a + gate with children A,B, deg_x(A+B) is at most max(deg_x A,deg_x B), with the zero polynomial assigned degree -infinity. This is at most occ_x(A)+occ_x(B). At a × gate, deg_x(AB) is at most deg_x(A)+deg_x(B), even if cancellation or zero divisors lower the degree or make the product zero. By induction this is at most occ_x(A)+occ_x(B). These sums are the parent’s occurrence count, proving the claim. Since deg_x(x^2)=2 in R[x], occurrence count at most one rules out equality.

statement: Lemma (bounded-depth unfolding). Let C be a finite arithmetic circuit over any commutative ring, with one designated output, fan-in at most two, and maximum gate depth d when input gates have depth zero. There is an arithmetic formula computing the same polynomial with at most 2^(d+1)-1 gate occurrences. Proof: recursively replace each use of a circuit gate by a fresh copy of its defining operation and recursively unfold its predecessors. The resulting expression tree has height at most d+1 and at most two children per node, hence at most 1+2+...+2^d = 2^(d+1)-1 nodes. Each copied gate applies the same ring operation to the same predecessor polynomials, so induction on depth shows the unfolded expression computes the original output polynomial. In particular, depth O(log s) yields a polynomial-size formula when s is the circuit size. This controls reuse for shallow circuits, but does not ensure read-once variables or an roABP-IPS_LIN refutation.

statement: statement: Lemma (quantitative exponential promise transfer). Let L_m be a source language slice and Π_m a promise problem. Suppose R_m maps every m-bit input to a promise input, is computed by a fan-in-2 circuit of size at most 2^{ρm}, and maps YES inputs of L_m to YES instances of Π_m and NO inputs to NO instances of Π_m. Suppose every fan-in-2 circuit deciding L_m has size at least 2^{δm}, where constants satisfy 0≤ρ<δ. Then every circuit correctly deciding Π_m on its promise has size at least 2^{δm}−2^{ρm}−O(1), and hence at least 2^{δm−1} for all sufficiently large m. Proof: Given a promise decider D of size d, compose D with R_m. Promise preservation makes D∘R_m decide L_m, and the composed circuit has size at most d+2^{ρm}+O(1). The source lower bound implies 2^{δm}≤d+2^{ρm}+O(1), so d≥2^{δm}−2^{ρm}−O(1). Since ρ<δ, the subtracted term and constant are at most 2^{δm−1} for all sufficiently large m. The conclusion is conditional on the stated two-sided reduction and source lower bound; it does not construct either. statement: statement: Lemma. For a fixed deterministic single-tape machine M that halts within T(m)>=m steps on every m-bit input, the Boolean function computed by M has a fan-in-2 circuit of size O(T(m)^2). Proof: During T steps at most O(T) tape cells are visited, so a configuration has O(T) bits. The local transition from one configuration to the next is computed by O(T) fan-in-2 gates, since each cell update depends on its local symbol and the finite control/head information. Unrolling this transition circuit for T steps gives O(T^2) gates; selecting the output from the final configuration adds at most O(T^2) gates. Thus the total is O(T^2).

statement: statement: Lemma (explicit single-tape tableau simulation). Fix a deterministic single-tape Turing machine M with finite tape alphabet and finite state set. For each input length m, suppose M halts within T>=m steps, and its output is a Boolean string of length at most T, with each output bit determined by the final configuration. Then the output function has a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of size O(T^2). Proof: Use a window of O(T) tape cells containing every cell reachable within T steps. Encode each cell by a constant number of bits indicating its tape symbol and whether the head is there, together with the machine state in the marked cell. The initial encoding is wired from the input and constants. For each time step, each cell's next encoding is a Boolean function of that cell and its two neighbors' encodings, because M has a fixed local transition rule; this function has constant-size fan-in-2 implementation. Thus one transition layer has O(T) gates. Unroll T layers for O(T^2) gates. Each output bit specified by the final configuration is obtainable with O(T) gates by selecting among the O(T) cells, so at most T output bits add O(T^2) gates. Total size is O(T^2). This does not assert a reduction to Gap-MCSP or close any obligation unless G0002 is exactly this simulation-cost conversion.

statement: statement_start: Lemma (exact fiber criterion for a two-sided promise reduction). Let X be a finite source domain, L subset X, and let Y,N be disjoint target promise sides. A total map R:X->Z preserves the promise iff R(L) subset Y and R(X\L) subset N; merely having R(X) intersect both Y and N is insufficient. Proof: by definition, preservation requires every x in each source fiber to land in its designated side, giving the two inclusions; conversely, those inclusions imply preservation pointwise. For insufficiency, take X=Z={0,1}, L=Y={0}, N={1}, and R(0)=1,R(1)=0. Then R(X) hits both sides, but both fibers land on the wrong side. This finite lemma gives no complexity transfer or existence of a reduction.

statement: Lemma (finite-length promise reduction baseline). Let L be a nonconstant subset of {0,1}^m and let Pi=(Y,N) with nonempty disjoint Y,N subsets of {0,1}^q. Fix y in Y and z in N. There is a total fan-in-2 circuit R:{0,1}^m->{0,1}^q mapping L into Y and its complement into N with O(m 2^m + q) gates. Proof: For every a in L, form the minterm mu_a(x)=AND_{i=1}^m (x_i if a_i=1 else NOT x_i), using O(m) fan-in-2 gates. Let b(x)=OR_{a in L} mu_a(x), using O(|L|) further gates. Then b=1 iff x in L. For each coordinate j output (b AND y_j) OR ((NOT b) AND z_j), using O(1) gates. The output is y for x in L and z otherwise, hence preserves the promise. This gives a general finite-length baseline, but its exponential cost does not meet the efficient reduction needed by the bridge.

statement: Lemma (evaluator-size obstruction). Let L be a nonconstant language on {0,1}^m. Let R map each x to the truth table of a Boolean function f_x on n-bit inputs. Suppose one fan-in-2 circuit G(x,y) of size r computes f_x(y) for all x,y. If r <= s, then R cannot preserve the two sides of Gap-MCSP[s,s'] for any s' >= s, where YES consists of functions of circuit complexity at most s and NO of functions of complexity greater than s'. Proof: Since L is nonconstant, choose x outside L. Hardwire x into G to obtain a circuit for f_x of size at most r. Thus C(f_x) <= r <= s <= s', contradicting the requirement that this source NO input map to the NO side. This is a necessary-condition lemma only; it does not rule out reductions whose evaluator size exceeds s.

statement: Lemma (uniform evaluator simulation). Let R:{0,1}^m -> {0,1}^N be computed by a deterministic uniform algorithm in time T(m) on each input, with the output represented explicitly as N bits. Then R has a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of size O(T(m) log T(m)) (equivalently O(T(m)^2) under a direct tableau simulation). Consequently, if R is two-sided promise-preserving from a source slice L_m to promise problem (Y_m,N_m), and every circuit deciding L_m has size at least B(m), then every promise decider for (Y_m,N_m) has size at least B(m)-O(T(m) log T(m))-O(1). Proof: A deterministic T-step computation can be unrolled into a Boolean circuit simulating its time-space tableau; standard uniform-machine-to-circuit simulation gives size O(T log T) with a fixed finite machine alphabet and local transition rule. Compose this evaluator circuit with a promise decider D. The two-sided mapping property makes D∘R decide L_m. Its size is at most size(D)+O(T log T)+O(1), so B(m) is at most that quantity and rearrangement gives the bound. The bound is useful only when T(m) log T(m)=o(B(m)); the unresolved issue remains constructing such a two-sided R to Gap-MCSP/Gap-MKtP.

statement: Lemma (quadratic evaluator-cost transfer). Fix a deterministic multitape Turing machine M and input length m. Suppose M computes a total map R_m:{0,1}^m -> {0,1}^{N(m)} in at most T(m) steps on every input, with its output written explicitly. If R_m maps L_m into the YES side and its complement into the NO side of a promise problem, and every fan-in-2 circuit deciding L_m has at least B(m) gates, then every fan-in-2 circuit D deciding that promise problem on its promise has size at least B(m)-O((T(m)+m)^2)-O(1). Proof: In T steps M visits at most O(T+m) cells on each of its fixed number of tapes. Encode each cell's symbol and head status, and the finite control, with a constant number of bits. Each cell's next encoding is a fixed Boolean function of its bounded neighborhood and the finite control, so it has a constant-size fan-in-2 circuit. Unrolling T layers over O(T+m) cells gives O(T(T+m)) gates, which is O((T+m)^2). The output wires represent R_m(x). Composing this circuit with D decides L_m by the two promise-mapping conditions, with size size(D)+O((T+m)^2)+O(1). The source lower bound implies the stated inequality. This transfer is asymptotically useful when (T(m)+m)^2=o(B(m)). This statement uses the robust quadratic simulation; it does not assert a generic O(T log T) bound.

statement: Lemma (explicit-output necessary cost for quadratic transfer). Let R_m be computed by a deterministic machine in T(m) steps and output an explicit N(m)-bit string. Then N(m)<=O(T(m)) (for a standard machine writing at most a constant number of output symbols per step). Under the quadratic evaluator-cost transfer, the resulting promise lower bound is B(m)-O((T(m)+m)^2). Therefore this transfer yields an unbounded positive lower bound only if B(m)-O((T(m)+m)^2) is unbounded; in particular, a sufficient asymptotic regime is T(m)+m=o(sqrt(B(m))). If N(m) is not o(sqrt(B(m))), the quadratic transfer alone cannot establish a positive asymptotic lower bound. Proof: writing N output symbols takes Omega(N) steps, so T=Omega(N). Substitution into the stated transfer cost gives the necessary scale test; the sufficient condition makes the subtracted quadratic term o(B). This is a limitation of this transfer bound, not a nonexistence result for reductions or other proofs.

Suppose a total map R:{0,1}^m→{0,1}^N preserves both sides: R(x)∈Y for x∈L and R(x)∈N for x∉L. Suppose each output bit R_i is computed by a fan-in-2 circuit of size at most q. statement: statement: Lemma (complexity characterization for two fixed endpoints). Let L subset {0,1}^m be nonconstant, and let y,z be distinct q-bit strings in the YES and NO sides, respectively, of a promise problem. Let C(L) be the minimum fan-in-2 circuit size deciding L. Among total maps R:{0,1}^m -> {y,z} that map L to y and its complement to z, the minimum circuit size is C(L)+O(1), with an additive constant independent of q. Proof: Given a size-C(L) decider h, output y_j or z_j at coordinate j when they agree, and otherwise output h or NOT h according to y_j; constants, wires, and fan-out are free, so this costs C(L)+O(1). Conversely, since y != z, choose a coordinate j with y_j != z_j. For any such R, its j-th output equals 1_L or its complement. A single NOT if needed turns that output into a decider for L, so C(L) <= size(R)+1. Combining bounds proves the characterization. The result applies only when every output is one of these two fixed endpoints; general promise reductions may use many outputs and this argument gives no source lower bound for them.

statement_start: Lemma. Let L be a language and (Y,N) a promise problem with polynomial-length YES certificates verifiable in polynomial time on all inputs in Y. If for every input length m there is a polynomial-size fan-in-2 circuit R_m mapping x in L to Y and x not in L to N, then L is in NP/poly.
evidence: Proof: use the description of R_m as polynomial advice. Compute z=R_m(x), guess a polynomial-length certificate for z, and run the verifier. Completeness on Y accepts some certificate for every x in L. Soundness on N rejects all certificates for every x outside L. The circuit advice and verification are polynomial, giving an NP/poly machine. Scope requires completeness on Y and soundness on N, not merely a verifier sound on all inputs outside Y.

statement:
statement: Sparse-slice circuit upper bound. Fix integers n≥1 and k≥0, and any set A⊆{0,1}^n with |A|≤n^k. The characteristic function of A has a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of size O(n^{k+1}). Proof: For each a∈A, construct the equality test E_a(x)=∧_{i=1}^n (x_i if a_i=1, else ¬x_i), using at most n negations and n−1 binary AND gates. Form the OR of all E_a using at most |A|−1 binary OR gates; for A empty use the constant-zero circuit. This circuit accepts exactly A and has size at most |A|(2n−1)+|A|−1=O(n^{k+1}).
proof: As stated: each E_a accepts precisely the input a, so their disjunction accepts precisely the elements of A. The gate count is linear in n per element plus the disjunction tree, hence at most |A|(2n−1)+max(0,|A|−1), which is O(n^{k+1}).

structure.evidence: Constructive quantitative form of the sparse-slice obstruction already recorded as S-da12fd2c9f: ordinary fan-in-2 circuit lower bounds superpolynomial in n cannot hold for a slice containing at most n^k strings. This does not establish any transfer to a different resource model.

label: S0054
statement:
statement: Polynomial-sparse target composition. Suppose A_n is a subset of {0,1}^{N(n)}, |A_n|≤N(n)^k for fixed k, N(n) is polynomial in n, and R_n:{0,1}^n→{0,1}^{N(n)} has polynomial-size fan-in-2 circuits. Then f_n(x)=1 iff R_n(x)∈A_n has polynomial-size fan-in-2 circuits.
proof: For each y∈A_n, test equality R_n(x)=y by comparing its N(n) output bits, using O(N(n)) gates. OR these tests over A_n, using O(|A_n|) gates. The resulting circuit computes f_n and has size O(N(n)(|A_n|+1))+size(R_n), which is polynomial in n under the hypotheses. Thus polynomial-size reductions into polynomially sparse fixed-length slices cannot transfer a superpolynomial ordinary circuit lower bound to the source.
evidence: Composes the explicit equality-test circuit with the reduction, making the sparse-slice obstruction apply directly to this bridge form. Transfers to other resource models remain open.

label: S0055
statement: statement: Lemma (quadratic circuit simulation for bounded-time output maps). Fix a deterministic Turing machine M with a fixed number of tapes, fixed finite alphabet, and fixed transition rule. Suppose on every input x of length m, M halts within t(m) steps and leaves its N(m)-bit output on a designated tape, with N(m)=O(t(m)) and t(m)>=m. Then the map x -> output(M,x) is computed by a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of size O(t(m)^2). Proof: Only O(t) tape cells can be visited in t steps. Encode the symbols, head markers, and finite control state of each configuration with O(t) bits. The initial configuration bits are constants or input bits. Given one encoded configuration, each cell's next symbol and each head marker are determined by its current symbol, its adjacent head markers, and the finite control state; the fixed transition rule realizes these updates with O(1) fan-in-2 gates per cell (broadcasting the finite control bits costs at most O(t) gates per layer). Thus one transition layer has O(t) gates, and t layers have O(t^2) gates. Make halting configurations stationary and read the designated output cells at the final layer; this requires O(N)=O(t) additional gates. This proves the stated bound.

label: S0002
statement: REPAIRED LEMMA (window + Sperner atom bound, exact scope). Setting: integer weights w_1..w_n, threshold t, restriction R in which each variable is independently free (prob 1/3), fixed to 0 (1/3) or fixed to 1 (1/3). Let F = free set, G = fixed set, Y = sum of w_j over fixed-1 j, b_j in {0,1} the fixed values, s = #{j in G: w_j != 0}, W_F = sum_{j in F} (max(0,w_j) - min(0,w_j)), mn_F = sum_{j in F} min(0,w_j), mx_F = sum_{j in F} max(0,w_j). Claim: P(gate nonconstant | F) <= min(1, W_F * C(s, floor(s/2)) / 2^s) <= min(1, W_F / sqrt(s)) for s >= 1. Proof. (1) Gate g = [sum_F x_j w_j + Y >= t] over free x. Its value set over free x is {0,1} iff mn_F + Y < t <= mx_F + Y, i.e. Y in (t - mx_F, t - mn_F - 1]... precisely iff t - Y in (mn_F, mx_F]. This interval contains exactly W_F integers, so P(nonconst | F) = P(Y in a set of W_F integers). (2) Erdos (1945) / Sperner: for nonzero integers |w_j| >= 1, j in G, each value y is attained by at most C(s, floor(s/2)) subsets of G; hence P(Y = y) <= C(s,floor(s/2))/2^s for every y. (3) Union bound over the W_F integers gives the first inequality; min with 1 is trivial. (4) C(s,floor(s/2))/2^s <= 1/sqrt(s) for s >= 1 (standard central-binomial bound). Scope: exact for every integer weight vector and threshold; the 1/3-model enters only through the law of F. Consequence (decay regime): if W_F = o(sqrt(s)) then P(nonconst | F) -> 0. For unit weights this is f = o(sqrt(n)) free variables. At constant free fraction it gives NO decay (E[W_F] ~ n/3 >> sqrt n), consistent with cm-64653810efde4130.

label: S0013
statement: PROOF. (a) Read set R = inputs reachable from the output. The cone of the output has g <= S gates and |R| input nodes; it is connected; each gate has at most 2 incoming edges, so edges <= 2g. Connectivity gives |R| + g - 1 <= 2g, so |R| <= g + 1 <= S + 1. (b) Let U = complement of R, u = |U| = N - |R|. Let T0 be the zero table (YES, distance 0 from the zero circuit). Let T be zero on R and uniform on U. C does not read U, so C(T) = C(T0) = 1. (c) Fix g in Y. dist(T,g) >= dist_U(T,g), and dist_U(T,g) ~ Bin(u,1/2) (T_i differs from g_i with prob 1/2, independent). If u >= 4D, Hoeffding gives Pr[dist_U <= D] <= Pr[Bin(u,1/2) <= u/4] <= exp(-u/8). (d) Union bound over Y (|Y| <= M): Pr[exists g in Y with dist(T,g) <= D] <= M exp(-u/8). If u >= 4D and u > 8 ln M, this is < 1, so with positive probability T is NO and C(T) = 0, contradicting C(T) = 1. Therefore u < max(4D, 8 ln M). (e) S >= |R| - 1 = N - u - 1 > N - 1 - max(4D, 8 ln M). Counting: M bounds the number of circuits with at most s gates (choose s gates, each with 2 predecessors among <= N+s nodes and one of 16 ops; sum over sizes <= s gives the factor s+1).

structure.gap: Scope and status: this is a LINEAR bound, N - O(N^(1-eps) + m^(c+1)). It does not reach G0001 (size N(log N)^k for general circuits) nor G0002. The constant is no better than S0002 (N-1). The read-set method cannot give superlinear bounds, because the only circuit fact used is S >= |R| - 1 and |R| <= N. structure.lemma: REPAIRED K-L (exact). Setting: N = 2^m positions, s = m^c, 0 < eps < 1, D = N^(1-eps). Y = set of truth tables of B_2 circuits (fan-in 2, any binary op, unary and constant gates allowed) with at most s gates on N inputs. Promise problem: YES if dist(T,Y) <= D; NO if dist(T,Y) > D. Claim: every B_2 circuit C of size S that outputs 1 on YES and 0 on NO satisfies S >= N - 1 - max(4D, 8 ln M), where M = (s+1)(16(N+s)^2)^s, and ln M = O(s log N) = O(m^(c+1)). Hence S >= N - O(N^(1-eps) + m^(c+1)). Exact MCSP circuits solve this promise problem (YES tables lie in Y, promise NO tables are exact NO tables), so the bound transfers to exact MCSP[m^c].

label: S0020
statement: LEMMA D1 (base gate elimination, free negations and constants). Let f: {0,1}^n -> {0,1} be nonconstant and not a literal, and let C be an optimal fan-in-2 B_2 circuit for f with s >= 1 gates. Some input x_i feeds a gate g = op(x_i, h) with h a gate or input, since f depends on some variable and every variable read is read by some gate. Fix x_i = b. Then g computes a function of h alone: a constant, h, or NOT h. Deleting g and redirecting its consumers to h or to a constant, with negations absorbed into consumers (free negations), gives a circuit for f|x_i=b with at most s-1 gates. Hence some restriction x_i = b has C(f|x_i=b) <= C(f) - 1. Proof is complete for this statement. It is the base step of gate elimination and gives drop >= 1 only. It does not yield drop >= 2 (cm-cdb2df6cc1874b4e shows max drop 1 for 32 non-literal 3-variable functions), and iterating it gives only the linear bound already in S0002.

structure.evidence: Proof from definitions; consistent with cm-cdb2df6cc1874b4e (max drop >= 1 on every non-literal 3-variable function, checked there). Not submitted for validation. Does NOT close G0001 or G0002.
structure.gap: G0001 and G0002 remain open. Superlinear general-circuit bounds need a restriction-stable argument forcing two gates to die per restriction, which the single-variable fan-in argument cannot supply. Known gate-elimination for explicit functions stops near 3n (Find-Golovnev-Hirsch-Kulikov 2016/2023, recalled from memory, not source-checked this session), so this route does not reach N(log N)^k for MCSP.

label: S0061
statement: LEMMA L3 (m=3 base step for gate elimination). Let f: {0,1}^3 -> {0,1} have exact B2 size s(f) >= 3, where B2 = all 16 binary gates, inputs and constants free, size = number of gates. Then there exist i in {1,2,3} and b in {0,1} such that g = f restricted to x_i=b is non-constant and not a literal, s(g) = 1, and hence s(f) - s(g) >= 2. PROOF. (a) g depends on at most 2 variables. (b) Any non-constant, non-literal function of two variables x,y is a binary function of (x,y), and the 16 gates cover all 16 binary functions, so one gate computes it; zero gates are impossible because inputs and constants are free and not gates. Hence s(g) = 1 for such g. (c) EXISTENCE: every f with s(f) >= 3 has a restriction of the non-constant, non-literal type. This step is a finite check over the 104 functions with s >= 3, done by cm-55baaaf072424646 (min over f of max drop with restricted size 1 is 2 at s=3 and 3 at s=4). It is NOT yet a hand proof. Consequence: the drop-2 base case holds for m=3 with restricted functions of size exactly 1, conditional on (c) being checked. SCOPE: m=3 only; no general-m statement.

label: S0062
statement: LEMMA L3' (hand proof of existence step (c) of L3, m=3). Setting: f: {0,1}^3 -> {0,1}, s(f) = exact B2 circuit size (all 16 binary gates, inputs and constants free). Call a function of 2 variables 'full' if it depends essentially on both. CLAIM: if s(f) >= 3 then some restriction x_i=b gives a FULL 2-variable function g, and then s(g) = 1. PROOF. (1) If f depends essentially on at most 2 variables, s(f) <= 1, because every 2-variable function is a binary gate applied to two inputs or a constant/literal (size 0 or 1). So s(f) >= 3 implies f depends essentially on x, y, z. (2) Fix x. If f|x=0 or f|x=1 depends essentially on both y and z, that restriction is FULL, done. (3) Otherwise each cofactor depends on at most one of y,z. Since f depends on y and z essentially, y lies in the dependence set of some cofactor and so does z. Hence one cofactor depends essentially on y only, the other on z only: f|x=0 = h0(y), f|x=1 = h1(z), with h0 and h1 non-constant. (4) Restrict y=c (c in {0,1}), giving g(x,z) = (not x)*h0(c) OR x*h1(z), with h0(c) in {0,1} a constant and h1 non-constant. If h0(c)=0, g = x AND h1(z), which depends essentially on x (since h1 takes value 1 somewhere) and on z. If h0(c)=1, g = (not x) OR h1(z), which again depends essentially on x and z. So g is FULL. (5) A FULL 2-variable g is not constant and not a literal, so s(g) >= 1, and it is computed by one binary gate (the 16 gates give all 16 binary functions), so s(g) = 1. Hence s(f) - s(g) = s(f) - 1 >= 2. Also s(g) <= s(f) because restricting an input to a constant in a circuit does not increase the gate count. QED. This is a hand proof: it replaces the finite check that was the gap of step (c). CONSEQUENCE: L3 is now fully proved for m=3 (parts a, b by hand, part c here). SCOPE: m=3 only, B2 circuits, exact size. It does NOT give a general-m lower bound: gate elimination with a drop of 2 per restriction gives only linear bounds, and the step does not extend to restricted functions of size >= 2 that appear for m >= 4.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA L3' (hand proof of existence step (c) of L3, m=3). Setting: f: {0,1}^3 -> {0,1}, s(f) = exact B2 circuit size (all 16 binary gates, inputs and constants free). Call a function of 2 variables 'full' if it depends essentially on both. CLAIM: if s(f) >= 3 then some restriction x_i=b gives a FULL 2-variable function g, and then s(g) = 1. PROOF. (1) If f depends essentially on at most 2 variables, s(f) <= 1, because every 2-variable function is a binary gate applied to two inputs or a constant/literal (size 0 or 1). So s(f) >= 3 implies f depends essentially on x, y, z. (2) Fix x. If f|x=0 or f|x=1 depends essentially on both y and z, that restriction is FULL, done. (3) Otherwise each cofactor depends on at most one of y,z. Since f depends on y and z essentially, y lies in the dependence set of some cofactor and so does z. Hence one cofactor depends essentially on y only, the other on z only: f|x=0 = h0(y), f|x=1 = h1(z), with h0 and h1 non-constant. (4) Restrict y=c (c in {0,1}), giving g(x,z) = (not x)*h0(c) OR x*h1(z), with h0(c) in {0,1} a constant and h1 non-constant. If h0(c)=0, g = x AND h1(z), which depends essentially on x (since h1 takes value 1 somewhere) and on z. If h0(c)=1, g = (not x) OR h1(z), which again depends essentially on x and z. So g is FULL. (5) A FULL 2-variable g is not constant and not a literal, so s(g) >= 1, and it is computed by one binary gate (the 16 gates give all 16 binary functions), so s(g) = 1. Hence s(f) - s(g) = s(f) - 1 >= 2. Also s(g) <= s(f) because restricting an input to a constant in a circuit does not increase the gate count. QED. This is a hand proof: it replaces the finite check that was the gap of step (c). CONSEQUENCE: L3 is now fully proved for m=3 (parts a, b by hand, part c here). label: S0082
statement: LEMMA L-LEAF (connectivity count, proof complete). Let C be a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit over the basis B2 with g gates computing f, and let E(f) be the set of essential variables of f. Then |E(f)| <= s(f) + 1, where s(f) is the exact B2 size. Proof: (1) Every essential variable x of f is a leaf of C, since otherwise f would not depend on x. Let L be the number of leaves in the cone of the output; then E(f) is contained in those L leaves, so |E(f)| <= L. (2) Let V be the set of gates plus leaves of the output cone; every node of V reaches the output, so the undirected graph (V, edges) is connected. (3) Each gate has at most 2 incoming edges, so |edges| <= 2g. (4) A connected graph has at least |V| - 1 = g + L - 1 edges. Hence g + L - 1 <= 2g, i.e. L <= g + 1. (5) Therefore |E(f)| <= L <= g + 1. Minimising over C gives |E(f)| <= s(f) + 1. Consequence: any restriction-drop argument of the S0080 type, after composition, returns at most this bound; it is linear in the number of variables and gives no superlinear bound. Status: bookkeeping, not progress. It closes no obligation (G0001 and G0002 stay open).

structure.lemma: REPAIR of S0005 union bound (Lemma K-L). Let N = 2^m, and let Circ(N,s) be the set of fan-in-2 B2 circuits on N input variables with at most s gates (unary gates and constants allowed). Claim: |Circ(N,s)| <= (16 (N+s)^2)^s, so log2 |Circ(N,s)| <= s (4 + 2 log2(N+s)) = O(s log N). Proof: label the nodes 1..N (inputs) and N+1..N+s (gates in topological order). Gate N+i chooses an ordered pair of earlier nodes (at most (N+i-1)^2 choices) and one of 16 binary functions, so the number of gate-lists is at most prod_{i=1}^{s} 16 (N+i-1)^2 <= (16 (N+s)^2)^s. The output is one of at most N+s nodes, a factor that is absorbed in the same bound. Consequence for s = m^c and log N = m: log2 |Circ| = O(m^c * m) = O(m^{c+1}). The refuted step gave O(m^c log m); the correct exponent is m^{c+1} because log N = m, not log m. The repaired statement, with the S0087 connectivity fact (a circuit reading R inputs has at least |R|-1 gates), is: CC_B2(N^{-eps}-MCSP[m^c]) >= N - O(N^{1-eps} + m^{c+1}), using Hoeffding deviation with t = O(m^{c+1}) and a union bound over the 2^{O(m^{c+1})} circuits. This is the same linear bound as G0003; it does not change the scope.

statement: LEMMA T (decision-to-search transfer; a bookkeeping reduction, NOT progress, closes no obligation). Setup: N=2^m, s=m^c with c>=1 fixed; MCSP[s] is the decision problem on truth tables of length N with threshold s; search-MCSP[s] is as in McKay-Murray-Williams STOC 2019 Thm 1.4 with empty oracle A (A=empty is in PH). Claim: there is a constant e=e(c) such that if MCSP[s] has no general fan-in-2 circuits of size N*(log N)^(e+1), of any depth, then search-MCSP[s] has no circuits of size N*poly(s) and depth poly(s), and hence NP is not in P/poly by MMW19 Thm 1.4 bullet 3 (s(n)>=n holds since s=m^c>=m). Proof: let C be a search circuit of size S=N*poly(s) and depth D=poly(s). Build a decision circuit: (i) run C on x to get a candidate circuit description of size O(s log s), or bottom; (ii) evaluate the candidate on all N inputs with a universal circuit of size poly(s) per input (valid since m<=s, so input indices fit in poly(s) bits); (iii) compare the N outputs with x and AND them, depth log N. Correctness on every x follows from correctness of the search problem: it outputs a circuit exactly when one of size <=s computes x, and bottom otherwise. The decision circuit has size S + N*poly(s) = N*(log N)^(e) and depth D + poly(s) + log N. Taking k >= e+1 in the decision hypothesis contradicts this, so the decision lower bound with k=e+1 implies the search hypothesis of MMW Thm 1.4 bullet 3.

label: S0124
statement: R1432-L1: Over B2 (all 16 binary gates, free input and output negation), every circuit computing XOR_n for n >= 2 has at least n-1 gates, with equality attained by the XOR chain. Proof: take a minimum circuit with g gates. (i) Every gate has two distinct input wires, since a gate with equal or constant inputs computes a unary function and can be bypassed with a free negation, contradicting minimality. (ii) Every gate is an ancestor of the output, otherwise it is deleted. (iii) Every x_i is an ancestor of the output, since XOR_n depends on all n variables. So the n+g nodes (inputs and gates) are connected in the undirected graph G. (iv) G has exactly 2g edges, one per gate input slot. A connected multigraph on n+g nodes has at least n+g-1 edges, so 2g >= n+g-1, giving g >= n-1. Verified exactly for n=2,3,4 by cm-dcbd9d8d03e94e6d (sizes 1,2,3). Status: a known folklore bound (cite Redkin 1973 as the source to check), not new.

label: S0145
statement: LEMMA (cost-2 case of H_B, all n, B2 with free inputs and constants): if f: {0,1}^n -> {0,1} has exact B2 cost 2, there exist variables x != y and values a,b such that f|x=a,y=b is a constant or a positive literal, so the restriction drops the cost by exactly 2. PROOF: a cost-2 circuit is f=t(p,q) with p=t'(u,v) of cost 1 and q a leaf (or the mirror); essential variables lie in {u,v,q}, and a two-variable function has cost <= 1, so f has exactly 3 essential variables x,y,z with p=t'(x,y), q=z. t' is non-constant, so p takes both values 0,1. Let F_c = t(c,z), c in {0,1}. Since p and z are both essential, F_0 != F_1 and f is not a function of p alone. Among the possible pairs {F_0,F_1} of functions of z in {0,1,z,not z}, the pair {const,const} is excluded (then f=p, which ignores z), so some F_c is z or a constant. statement: LEMMA (decision-to-search transfer, A = empty oracle; repairs S0106). Let N = 2^n, s(n) = n^c, c >= 1 fixed. Suppose for some fixed k' no general Boolean circuit of size N(log N)^k' decides MCSP[n^c] on length N (for infinitely many n). Then search-MCSP[s] on length N has no circuits of size N*poly(s) and depth poly(s). PROOF: assume a search circuit S of size N*n^d and depth n^d exists. On input T, S outputs either a flag NO or a description w of a circuit C_T with at most s gates (O(s log s) bits). Decision circuit: compute w from T with S; evaluate the circuit described by w on all 2^n inputs with a universal evaluator (N*poly(s) gates, poly(s) depth); compare the 2^n outputs with T bitwise (N gates); output 1 iff the flag is not NO and all N comparisons agree. Total size N*poly(s) = N*poly(log N) since poly(s) = poly(n) = poly(log N), and the circuit is correct: T has a circuit of size <= s iff S's output C_T computes T. Contrapositive gives the bullet-3 hypothesis for A = empty oracle in PH. The degree of the polynomial is absorbed by quantifying over all k, so no constant e(c) depends on the poly degree. KNOWN-RESULT CHECK: this uses only MMW Thm 1.4 bullet 3 (exact hypothesis above) and the owner note that a decision lower bound suffices a fortiori. OPEN POINT: this reduction does not supply the decision lower bound itself, which is the open obligation.

label: S0151
statement: LEMMA T' (flag-bit transfer; repairs S0106 and supersedes its step (ii)-(iii)). Source (MMW STOC19 p.1, verbatim): search-MCSP^A[s(n)] takes a truth table T of size N=2^n and outputs a circuit of size at most s(n) with AND, OR, NOT, A-oracle gates, 'or report that no such circuit exists'. Claim: let s(n)=n^c, A empty. If search-MCSP^empty[s] is computed by circuits of size S and depth D whose output includes the report bit b, then MCSP[s] (decision) has circuits of size S+O(1) and depth D. Proof: b=1 iff no circuit of size <= s computes T, so NOT b is the decision bit, a single output of the same circuit. Repair of the degree issue: if search size is N*poly(s) = N*(log N)^{O(c d)} for a polynomial of degree d, then with k = c d + 1 the decision circuit has size <= N (log N)^k for large N. Hence H (for every fixed k, infinitely often no MCSP[m^c] circuit of size N(log N)^k) gives: for infinitely many n, search-MCSP^empty[s] has no N*poly(s)-size, poly(s)-depth circuits. Then MMW Thm 1.4 bullet 3 (A empty is in PH, s(n) >= n) gives NP not in P/poly. The constant e(c) is not needed.

statement: Repair candidate for the cost-3 drop step is vacuous. Let f be an exact formula of cost 3 (3 binary gates, at most 4 leaves, depends on at most 4 variables). For any two essential variables x_i, x_j and any a,b in {0,1}, f restricted to x_i=a, x_j=b depends on at most 2 variables. label: S0171
statement: Single-variable gate elimination (B2 circuits): if C has size s and some gate g takes x_i as input, then C|x_i=a has size <= s-1 for each a in {0,1}. Proof: under x_i=a, g becomes a constant, y or not-y; delete g and absorb the constant or negation into consumers (B2 gates absorb constants and negated inputs by changing their truth table); a consumer that becomes constant or unary is deleted by the same rule; if g is the output the size is 0. No new gates are added. Each deletion removes one gate.

label: S0217
statement: S-R1736-T-prime: LEMMA T' (repair of S0106, closes gap G0153). Setup: N = 2^m, s = m^c, c >= 1 fixed; search-MCSP[s] and MCSP[s] are as in MMW19 STOC 2019, with oracle A = empty (A in PH). Hypothesis H_dec: for every fixed k, MCSP[m^c] has no general fan-in-2 circuits of size N (log N)^k, of any depth. Claim: H_dec implies that for every polynomial p, search-MCSP[m^c] has no circuits of size N p(s) and depth p(s); hence NP not in P/poly by MMW19 Thm 1.4 bullet 3 (valid since s = n^c >= n). Proof: (1) Let C be a search circuit of size N p(s), depth p(s), with input x in {0,1}^N. Its output is a description D(x) of O(s log s) bits, or the symbol bottom. (2) Build the decision circuit: for each index i in [N], feed D(x) and the hard-wired index i into a universal evaluator U for circuits of size s on m inputs; U has size poly(s) and depth poly(s) (standard O(s log s) universal circuit, gate descriptions as wires). (3) Output bit i of the candidate is compared with x_i; AND the N comparisons; if D(x) = bottom, output 0. (4) Correctness: if the search output is a circuit of size <= s computing x, the comparisons all succeed and the output is 1; if x has no circuit of size <= s, search outputs bottom, so output 0; a circuit of size <= s computing x exists iff search outputs a valid description. (5) Size: N p(s) + N poly(s) = N (log N)^{k(p)} for some k(p) depending only on p and c, since poly(s) = poly(log N). Depth: p(s) + poly(s) + O(log N) = poly(log N). (6) H_dec at k = k(p) is contradicted by this circuit. Since p is arbitrary, H_dec for every fixed k yields 'no search circuit of size N poly(s) and depth poly(s)'. QED. SCOPE: conditional reduction, A = empty, s = m^c. It needs the decision bound for every fixed k; a single k does not suffice, because the polynomial p given by NP in P/poly is not known in advance. It closes no obligation (the P2 obligation is the decision lower bound itself, still open). Classification: bookkeeping reduction, not progress toward P != NP; no LOWER_BOUND is claimed, so no perfect-matching or naturality test is required for this step.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (cost-2 pair restriction, general n; proves S0104 in general): Let f on {0,1}^n be nonconstant, not a literal, with exact B2 cost 2. Then there exist i != j and a,b in {0,1} such that f restricted to x_i=a, x_j=b is constant or a literal. Proof: a size-2 circuit has the form f = g(h(x_a,x_b), x_c) with h nondegenerate. If c in {a,b}, f depends only on x_a,x_b and fixing both gives a constant. If c not in {a,b}, fixing x_a,x_b to any values gives g(const, x_c), a unary function of x_c, hence constant or a literal.

label: S0239
statement: LEMMA BP (bottom-pair drop, exact B2, any n). Let f: {0,1}^n -> {0,1} have exact B2 cost s >= 2, and let C be an optimal circuit for f in which some gate g reads two distinct input variables x_i, x_j. Then for every a,b in {0,1}, the restriction rho: x_i=a, x_j=b satisfies cost(f|rho) <= s-2. PROOF. (1) g is not the output: otherwise f = op(x_i,x_j) has cost <= 1, contradicting s >= 2. So g has a successor h. (2) Under rho, g becomes the constant c = op(a,b). (3) h = op'(c,w) for its other input w (w may be g itself, a leaf or a gate). Then h is a unary function of w: a literal of w or a constant. (4) Delete h and redirect its successors to that literal or constant. B2 gate tables are closed under negation of inputs, so a negated literal is absorbed into the successor's table; a constant input turns the successor into a unary function, which is removed the same way. Each deletion removes one gate and never adds one. (5) Deleting g and h gives a circuit with at most s-2 gates computing f|rho. QED. SCOPE: exact B2 cost, any n, any f whose some optimal circuit has a bottom pair. It does NOT cover f whose every optimal circuit has every variable-reading gate joined to another gate, so general H_B remains OPEN. CONSEQUENCE: H_B holds for every f with a bottom-pair optimal circuit, including the cost-3 functions on 4 variables whose optimal circuits have a bottom pair. Gate elimination with a drop of 2 per two-variable restriction gives only a linear lower bound (size >= about n), so this is not progress toward the superpolylog target. Barrier label (diagnostic only): not relativizing or algebrizing in any meaningful sense; not natural, since it is a structural property of a circuit, not a constructive property of the truth table; localizing: no. Next: test on n=4 whether every size>=3 function has an optimal circuit with a bottom pair (exhaustive), since that decides whether LEMMA BP covers the cost-3 case without the BFS argument.

label: S0282
statement: REPAIR OF S0090 (linear only). Let m >= 1, N = 2^m, c >= 1, 0 < eps < 1, s = m^c, M = number of B2 circuits (16 gate types, fan-in 2, one designated output) on N inputs with at most s gates. Define the promise problem Gap-MCSP_D[s]: YES if the table lies within Hamming distance D of the truth table of some circuit of size <= s; NO if it lies at distance > D from all of them. Take D = N^{1-eps}. Then every B2 circuit C that decides Gap-MCSP_D[s] has size S >= N - 1 - max(4D, 8 ln M), and since ln M = O(s log(N+s)) = O(m^{c+1}), S >= N - O(N^{1-eps} + m^{c+1}). Proof: this is S0013 with its Y set taken as all circuits of size <= s. Read set R of the output cone has |R| <= S+1 (connectivity). Let U be the unread inputs, u = |U|. Let T = zero on R and uniform on U. C(T) = C(zero table) = 1 since C does not read U and the zero table is YES. For each g in Y, Hoeffding gives Pr[dist_U(T,g) <= D] <= exp(-u/8) when u >= 4D. A union bound over Y gives Pr[some g within D] <= M exp(-u/8) < 1 when u > 8 ln M. Then T is NO, so C(T) = 0, a contradiction. Hence u < max(4D, 8 ln M) and S >= |R| - 1 = N - u - 1. The essential-variable count in S0090(c) is thereby supplied by this argument. This is a linear bound with explicit error term, NOT superlinear and NOT a repair of the N(log N)^k target.

Known context: read-set arguments of this kind give at most about N for B2 circuits, and the best known general lower bounds for explicit functions are linear (about 3N, Find-Golovnev-Hirsch-Kulikov 2016, to be source-checked). Does not close G0001 (N(log N)^k) or G0002.

label: S0284
statement: ROUTE B LINK (reconstruction slice 2, read from MMW19 Sec. 5). Statement: let c>=1, s(n)=n^c, A = empty oracle. If for every k there are infinitely many n such that decision MCSP[s(n)] on N=2^n inputs has no B2 circuit (any depth) of size N*s(n)^k, then for every k there are infinitely many n such that search-MCSP^A[s(n)] has no circuit of size N*s(n)^k and depth s(n)^k; hence by MMW19 Thm 1.4 bullet 3, NP is not in P/poly. Proof: a search circuit outputs a circuit description of size <= s(n) or the symbol none; MCSP[s(n)](T)=1 iff the output is not none, which one OR over the O(s log s) output bits (or the flag bit, by the output convention) decides, adding O(s log s) <= N gates. So a search circuit of size N*s^k gives a decision circuit of size N*s^k + O(s log s) <= N*s^(k+1) for large n, contradicting the hypothesis with k+1. Bullet 3's proof (contrapositive via Lemma 3.1 with l(n)=s(n)^3) yields circuits at every n under NP in P/poly, so the infinitely-often form suffices. REVIEW: check the search output convention in MMW19 (Definition of search-MCSP) and the quantifier reading.

label: S0286
statement:
statement: Restriction recurrence for Boolean function circuit complexity in the B2 basis with constants allowed: for f(x,z)=f_x(z), where x is one input bit, max(C(f_0), C(f_1)) <= C(f) <= C(f_0)+C(f_1)+4. Consequently, if C(f)>s, then at least one restriction has complexity >(s-4)/2.
proof: Hardwiring x=0 or x=1 in a circuit for f computes the corresponding restriction without adding gates, so C(f_b)<=C(f). Conversely, take circuits for f_0 and f_1 and combine their outputs using (NOT x AND f_0) OR (x AND f_1). The B2 basis contains NOT, AND, and OR gates, so this adds four gates and computes f. Hence C(f)<=C(f_0)+C(f_1)+4. If both restrictions had complexity <=(s-4)/2, their sum plus four would be <=s, contradicting C(f)>s.

statement:
statement: For every m>=1 and Boolean functions f,g:{0,1}^m->{0,1} at Hamming distance t, |C(f)-C(g)| <= t(2m+4) in the B2 basis of fan-in-2 Boolean gates with gate-count size.
proof: List the t inputs where f and g differ as z_1,...,z_t. Define f_0=f and obtain f_i from f_{i-1} by toggling its value only at z_i. Then f_t=g. Each consecutive pair differs at exactly one input, so the single-entry sensitivity lemma gives |C(f_i)-C(f_{i-1})| <= 2m+4. By the triangle inequality, |C(f)-C(g)| <= sum_{i=1}^t |C(f_i)-C(f_{i-1})| <= t(2m+4). For t=0 the functions are identical and the bound is 0.

label: S0296
statement:
statement: In the full B2 basis of all binary Boolean gates with gate-count size, for m>=2 and Boolean functions f,g:{0,1}^m->{0,1} differing on t inputs, |C(f)-C(g)|<=mt. For m=1 the bound |C(f)-C(g)|<=2t holds.
proof: For m>=2, fix any input z in {0,1}^m. Construct its point indicator delta_z with m-1 binary gates: the first gate accepts exactly the prescribed values of x_1,x_2, and each later binary gate combines the current indicator with x_i, accepting exactly when both the current indicator and the prescribed value of x_i hold. Each such two-input Boolean operation is one gate in the full B2 basis. One additional XOR gate computes f XOR delta_z, which differs from f only at z. Thus C(g)<=C(f)+m for functions differing at one point; exchanging f,g gives the absolute bound. For t differing points, toggle them one at a time and apply the triangle inequality, obtaining mt. When m=1, delta_z is x or NOT x; each is implementable with at most one binary gate by duplicating x as both inputs, and one XOR gate toggles it, giving the stated 2t bound by the same argument.

statement: statement: Neighborhood transfer for MCSP thresholds in the full B2 gate-count model. Let m>=2, let C(h) be minimum circuit size over all binary Boolean gates, and let f,g:{0,1}^m->{0,1} differ on at most t truth-table entries. If C(f)>s+mt, then C(g)>s. Dually, if C(f)<=s-mt, then C(g)<=s. Proof: For each differing entry z, its indicator delta_z is computed with m-1 gates: one binary gate tests the prescribed values of x_1,x_2, then m-2 binary gates successively conjoin the prescribed values of the remaining inputs. One additional binary gate computes f XOR delta_z, so toggling one entry changes minimum size by at most m in either direction. Toggling the at most t differing entries successively and applying the triangle inequality gives |C(f)-C(g)|<=mt. Thus C(f)>s+mt implies C(g)>=C(f)-mt>s; and C(f)<=s-mt implies C(g)<=C(f)+mt<=s.

label: S0301
statement: statement: Lemma: Let F:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be nonconstant and invariant under a group of coordinate permutations acting transitively on the N coordinates. Then every coordinate is essential. Proof: nonconstancy gives two inputs with different values; along a path changing one coordinate at a time, some edge changes F, so coordinate i is essential. For any j, transitivity supplies a coordinate permutation sending i to j; invariance transports the witness edge and preserves its differing F-values. Therefore j is essential. Consequence: if F is computed by a fan-in-two circuit with g gates and all N inputs are essential, its output cone contains all N inputs. The connected cone has at most 2g edges and at least N+g-1 vertices, hence at least N+g-1 edges, so g>=N-1.

statement: statement: For integers n,g>=0, in the circuit model with n input wires, gates chosen from all 16 binary Boolean functions, and output any input or gate wire, the number of distinct Boolean functions computable with at most g gates is at most (g+1)(n+g+1)(16(n+g+1)^2)^g. Proof: For a circuit with exactly j gates, order its gates topologically. At gate i there are at most 16 choices of binary operation and at most (n+i-1)^2 choices of ordered input wires, hence at most [16(n+g+1)^2]^j gate lists. There are at most n+j<=n+g+1 choices of output wire. Thus the number of functions with exactly j gates is at most (n+g+1)[16(n+g+1)^2]^g. Summing this bound over j=0,...,g gives the claim. This counts encodings, so duplicate encodings of one function only make it an upper bound.

label: S0306
statement: statement: For every n>=1 and g>=0, the number of Boolean functions on n inputs computable by at most g gates from the full set of 16 binary Boolean operations is at most (g+1)(n+g+1)(16(n+g+1)^2)^g. Proof: Fix j<=g. A topological encoding of a j-gate circuit records, for each gate i, one of 16 operations and an ordered pair of wires chosen among the n+i-1 input or preceding-gate wires; it also records an output wire among n+j choices. Thus the number of descriptions is at most (n+j) product_{i=1}^j 16(n+i-1)^2, which is at most (n+g+1)[16(n+g+1)^2]^g. Summing over j=0,...,g gives the stated bound. Every such circuit has at least one description, and descriptions may collide in function, so this is an upper bound on distinct functions. The condition n>=1 ensures an output wire exists when j=0.

statement: In the full fan-in-two Boolean basis on m>=2 inputs, let C(f) be minimum gate count. If f and g differ at one truth-table input, then |C(f)-C(g)|<=m. Hence for M_{m,s}(f)=1 iff C(f)<=s, every truth table f whose value changes after flipping one bit satisfies s-m+1<=C(f)<=s+m.
proof: For the differing input z, its point indicator delta_z is the conjunction of m prescribed literals, computed in m-1 fan-in-two gates. One further binary Boolean gate computes f XOR delta_z=g, so C(g)<=C(f)+m. Interchanging f and g gives C(f)<=C(g)+m. If M changes, one of the two complexities is at most s and the other at least s+1; combining this with their difference at most m gives the claimed interval.

statement: statement: For every m>=2, consider fan-in-two DAG circuits over all 16 binary Boolean gates, with the m input wires free and with no constant wires supplied. Let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, and let f_0,f_1 be its restrictions at x_1=0 and x_1=1, viewed as functions on the remaining m-1 variables. If each f_b has a circuit of at most s gates in this same model, then f has a circuit of at most 2s+8 gates. Proof: Lift each cofactor circuit to the m-input model by ignoring x_1. If its output is a nonconstant gate output or an input wire, no adjustment is needed. If its output is constant 0 or 1, generate that constant using x_2: form NOT(x_2) with one gate, then x_2 AND NOT(x_2) for 0 or x_2 OR NOT(x_2) for 1 with one more gate. Each branch output is therefore available at cost at most s+2. Form NOT(x_1), AND it with the f_0 output, AND x_1 with the f_1 output, and OR the products. These four gates implement (NOT x_1 AND f_0) OR (x_1 AND f_1), which equals f on both slices. Total size is at most 2(s+2)+4=2s+8. This bounds individual function complexity and does not imply a lower bound for the MCSP decision function.

Moreover, every restriction of f obtained by fixing any set of input variables has support size at most t, so the same construction bounds every restricted function by tm-1 (free negations) or m+tm-1 (charged negations).
proof: Let A be the t accepting assignments. For each a in A, form its minterm by ANDing its m literals using m-1 binary AND gates. OR the t minterms using t-1 binary OR gates. This computes f and uses t(m-1)+(t-1)=tm-1 gates, excluding the input negations. If negations are charged, compute each of the m negated input literals once and share them across all minterms, adding at most m gates. For any restriction, each surviving accepting assignment is the projection of one or more elements of A; hence the restricted support has size at most |A|=t. Applying the same construction to the restricted function proves the stated restricted bounds. Thus if tm-1<=s, every such restriction is in MCSP[s] under free negations; if m+tm-1<=s, this holds when negations are charged.

For all f,g, |C(f)-C(g)|<=2m d_H(f,g). Consequently, if F_s(f)!=F_s(g), then both C(f) and C(g) belong to [s-2m d_H(f,g), s+2m d_H(f,g)]. Proof: For any row a, its indicator delta_a is computed by negating each input variable whose bit in a is zero, using at most m NAND self-gates, and ANDing the m resulting literals with m-1 gates. Appending one XOR gate to a circuit for h yields h XOR delta_a, which toggles exactly row a and costs at most 2m new gates. Toggle each differing row from f to g to obtain C(g)<=C(f)+2m d_H(f,g); reverse the roles to get the absolute-value inequality. If F_s(f)=1 and F_s(g)=0, then C(f)<=s<C(g); the inequality gives C(f)>s-2md and C(g)<=s+2md. If the labels are reversed, exchange f,g. This is an exact stability statement for individual truth-table complexity and a necessary condition on every label-changing restriction pair; it does not yield gate consumption or a lower bound for circuits computing F_s.

statement:
statement: Let m>=1 and f,g:{0,1}^m->{0,1} differ on D. Let T(D) be the number of nonempty prefixes of elements of D of lengths 0 through m-1. In the fan-in-two Boolean circuit model with free input wires and charged negations, C(g)<=C(f)+m+3T(D)+1.
proof: Compute each negated input literal once, at cost at most m gates. For every nonempty prefix p of length less than m, construct the indicator h_p of suffixes z such that pz is in D, in decreasing order of prefix length. At length m-1, h_p is either the remaining input bit, its negation, or a constant, requiring no gates beyond the shared negations. At a shorter prefix p, h_p=(¬x_{i+1}∧h_{p0})∨(x_{i+1}∧h_{p1}); empty children are represented by 0. This uses at most three fan-in-two gates per nonempty prefix. Hence h_empty, the indicator of D, costs at most m+3T(D). XOR it with a minimum circuit for f using one gate. Since f XOR 1_D equals g pointwise, the claimed circuit bound follows.

structure.evidence: A direct inductive circuit construction on the prefix trie; the proof accounts for shared negations and at most three binary gates at each nonempty internal prefix.

statement: statement: For every m>=1, s>=0, and Boolean functions f,g:{0,1}^m->{0,1} with C(f)<=s<C(g), where C is minimum fan-in-two gate count over all 16 binary Boolean gates with free inputs, d_H(f,g)>=ceil((s+1-C(f))/(2m)). Proof: For each input a on which f and g differ, form its indicator delta_a using at most m gates to negate needed literals and m-1 AND gates, then toggle the current output by one XOR gate. Thus each differing row changes a circuit into one for the next function using at most 2m gates. Applying this to all d_H(f,g) rows gives C(g)<=C(f)+2m d_H(f,g). Since C(g)>=s+1, rearranging yields the stated bound.

label: S0343
statement: statement: For every m>=1, Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, and a in {0,1}^m, in fan-in-two DAG circuits over all 16 binary gates with free input wires, |C(f(· xor a))-C(f)| <= |a|. Proof: Given a circuit for f, replace each input x_i by x_i when a_i=0 and by a single shared NOT(x_i) wire when a_i=1. Each needed negation costs one gate, so this computes x↦f(x xor a) using at most |a| additional gates. Since translation by a is an involution, applying the same construction to f(· xor a) gives the reverse inequality. Coordinate permutations cost zero gates by renaming free input wires. Consequently, for any threshold s, translations by a preserve MCSP[s] membership whenever C(f)<=s-|a|, and preserve nonmembership whenever C(f)>s+|a|. The transitive translation action therefore controls labels outside the threshold band but need not preserve labels inside it.

label: S0345
statement: In the fan-in-two DAG model with free input wires and all 16 binary Boolean gates, the parity function on m input bits has minimum circuit size m-1. For the upper bound, use a chain of m-1 XOR gates (and for m=1, the input itself). For the lower bound, take the output’s ancestor subgraph, including every input on which the output depends. It is connected and contains all m input vertices and k gate vertices, so it has at least m+k-1 edges. Each gate has at most two incoming edges, hence the subgraph has at most 2k edges. Thus 2k >= m+k-1 and k >= m-1. This exact cost is for an individual truth table, not a lower bound on the MCSP decision circuit.

structure.gap: This lemma may constrain the individual-function complexity boundary relevant to MCSP, but does not close the open obligation to prove a general Boolean circuit lower bound for MCSP[m^c]. The implication from individual truth-table circuit complexity to decision-circuit complexity remains open here.

statement: statement: For every m>=1, parity on m Boolean inputs has minimum fan-in-two DAG circuit size exactly m-1, when input wires are free and all 16 binary Boolean operations are allowed. Proof: A chain of m-1 XOR gates computes parity. Conversely, parity depends on all m inputs. In any circuit computing it, retain the ancestor subgraph of the output. This graph contains the m input vertices and k gate vertices and is connected. Every edge enters a gate, and each gate has at most two incoming edges, so the graph has at most 2k edges. A connected graph on m+k vertices has at least m+k-1 edges; hence 2k >= m+k-1 and k >= m-1.

label: S0347
statement: statement: For m>=2, in the fan-in-two DAG model over all 16 binary Boolean operations with free input wires and constants not free, fixing one input coordinate of an m-input function computed by at most s gates yields an (m-1)-input cofactor computed with at most s+1 gates. If constants are free, the cofactor uses at most s gates. Proof: Substitute the fixed bit for every occurrence of the restricted input. If constants are free, this adds no gates. Otherwise, since m>=2, choose a remaining input x_j. Generate the needed constant once: x_j XOR x_j gives 0, while NAND(x_j,x_j) gives 1. Reuse this wire at every substituted occurrence. All original gates remain and at most one gate was added; the resulting circuit computes the cofactor.

structure.evidence: Direct construction and gate count in the statement. This establishes only the YES-side restriction behavior; it gives no NO-side preservation and does not close the superlinear lower-bound gaps G0001 or G0002.

label: S0348
statement: statement: Let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, m>=2, and let f_0,f_1 be its cofactors on one input coordinate. In fan-in-two DAG circuits over all 16 Boolean binary operations with free inputs, C(f) <= C(f_0)+C(f_1)+3. Proof: take minimum circuits for f_0 and f_1 on the remaining variables; compute d=f_0 XOR f_1 with one gate, compute x AND d with one gate, and output f_0 XOR (x AND d) with one gate. For x=0 this is f_0; for x=1 it is f_1. Hence if C(f)>s, at least one cofactor has complexity >(s-3)/2.

structure.evidence: Three-gate XOR/AND identity gives the construction exactly. No open superlinear obligation is claimed closed; this only quantifies the threshold loss under one-coordinate restriction.

label: S0350
statement: For every m>=1 and every Boolean function f on {0,1}^m with Hamming weight w, its fan-in-two DAG circuit complexity over all binary Boolean operations, with free input wires, satisfies C(f) <= min{m + mw - 1, m + m(2^m-w) - 1} whenever the corresponding listed weight is positive; if w=0 or w=2^m, C(f)<=2. Proof: For w>=1, express f as the OR of the w minterms indexed by its accepting rows. Compute all m negated input literals once, form each minterm with m-1 AND gates, and combine the minterms with w-1 OR gates, totaling m+w(m-1)+(w-1)=m+mw-1. For 2^m-w>=1, apply the same construction to the complement ¬f using its 2^m-w accepting rows, then append one gate computing NOT of that output (NAND(z,z)); this gives at most m+m(2^m-w)-1+1 gates, and the slightly sharper symmetric bound m+m(2^m-w)-1 also follows by directly expressing f as the AND of the clauses excluding each zero row, sharing the m positive input literals and using m-1 gates per clause plus w0-1 gates to combine clauses, where w0=2^m-w. In the endpoint cases, constants are computed with at most two gates, e.g. x1 AND NOT(x1) and its negation. Therefore every table of weight w lies in MCSP[s] if either applicable upper bound is at most s. This gives an explicit inner region of MCSP[s] near both constant tables but makes no lower bound claim about the MCSP decision function.

statement:
statement: For every m>=1 and every nonempty A subseteq {0,1}^m, let t=|A| and let q be the number of coordinates i for which some a in A has a_i=0. In fan-in-two DAG circuits with free input wires and all 16 binary Boolean operations, the indicator of A has a circuit with at most q+tm-1 gates.
proof: Compute NOT x_i once for each of the q coordinates that occur as zero in at least one row of A. For each a in A, form the conjunction of its m literals, using x_i when a_i=1 and the already computed NOT x_i when a_i=0; a conjunction of m literals takes at most m-1 fan-in-two AND gates (and zero gates if m=1). OR the t resulting minterms using t-1 fan-in-two OR gates. On input x, the minterm indexed by a is 1 exactly when x=a, so their OR is 1 exactly on A. The gate count is q+t(m-1)+(t-1)=q+tm-1. For m=1 the same count holds, including the case A={1}, where q=0 and the output wire x_1 uses zero gates.

statement:
statement: For integers m>=2 and s>=1, in the fan-in-two DAG model with free input wires and all 16 binary Boolean gates, every truth table on m inputs whose support has size t<=floor((s+1)/m) is computable with at most s gates. Consequently MCSP[s] contains at least sum_{j=0}^{floor((s+1)/m)} binomial(2^m,j) distinct truth tables (provided s>=2, so the zero table is realizable).
proof: For a nonempty support A of size t, form one minterm for each accepting row: negate each required input literal (at most m gates total), AND the m literals in each minterm using m-1 gates, and OR the t minterms using t-1 gates. The resulting gate count is at most m+t(m-1)+(t-1)=mt+m-1, which is at most s whenever t<=floor((s+1)/m). The zero function is computed with two gates as x_1 AND NOT(x_1), and is included when s>=2. Distinct supports yield distinct truth tables, so summing the binomial counts gives the stated lower bound on the number of YES inputs.
scope: All m>=2 and s>=2 in the specified basis/cost convention; this is a count of explicitly certified YES truth tables and implies no MCSP decision-circuit lower bound.

statement: statement: For every m>=r>=0 and Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, every restriction rho fixing r distinct input variables to constants has cofactor f|rho on m-r variables satisfying C_{m-r}(f|rho)<=C_m(f), where C_d is minimum gate count in the fan-in-two B2 DAG model with free input wires. Proof: take a minimum B2 DAG computing f, replace each fixed input wire by its assigned constant, simplify gates whose values become constant, and delete gates no longer feeding the output. This yields a circuit for f|rho with no more gates. Consequently, MCSP_m[s] restricted to the subcube rho is contained in MCSP_{m-r}[s] for every integer s>=0. At s=m^c this only implies membership in MCSP_{m-r}[m^c], not MCSP_{m-r}[(m-r)^c], and gives no gate-drop lower bound.

label: S0355
statement: statement: For every m>=r with m-r>=1, every Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, and every restriction rho fixing r inputs, in the fan-in-two DAG model with all 16 binary Boolean gates, free surviving input wires, and no free constants, C_{m-r}(f|rho)<=C_m(f)+3. Proof: start from a minimum circuit for f and substitute each fixed input by its prescribed constant. Use any surviving input wire z as a seed. Compute NOT z by one NAND gate with both inputs z; compute 0 as z AND NOT z; compute 1 as NAND(0,0). These at most three shared gates provide both constants. Copy the original gates with fixed wires redirected to the corresponding shared constant gates, then delete unused gates. The resulting DAG computes the cofactor and has at most C_m(f)+3 gates. Hence C_m(f)<=s implies C_{m-r}(f|rho)<=s+3. This does not imply membership in MCSP_{m-r}[(m-r)^c] when s=m^c.

Proof: start from a minimum circuit for f and substitute each fixed input by its prescribed constant. Use any surviving input wire z as a seed. Compute NOT z by one NAND gate with both inputs z; compute 0 as z AND NOT z; compute 1 as NAND(0,0). These at most three shared gates provide both constants. Copy the original gates with fixed wires redirected to the corresponding shared constant gates, then delete unused gates. The resulting DAG computes the cofactor and has at most C_m(f)+3 gates. Hence C_m(f)<=s implies C_{m-r}(f|rho)<=s+3. This does not imply membership in MCSP_{m-r}[(m-r)^c] when s=m^c.
structure.refuted_approach: S0354 as stated (C_{m-r}(f|rho)<=C_m(f) with free input wires but no free constants) is false. Counterexample: m=2, f(x,y)=x has C_2(f)=0; fixing x=0 gives the constant-zero function on the remaining input y, which requires at least one gate because a zero-gate output must be a free input wire.

label: S0357
statement:
statement: Let C be a fan-in-two DAG circuit with s gates over all 16 Boolean binary operations, free input wires and unrestricted fan-out, computing f on m input bits. For any input coordinate i and b in {0,1}, the restricted function f|_{x_i=b} has a circuit in the same model with at most s gates.
proof: Order C's gates topologically. Substitute the constant b for every occurrence of input x_i. Process each gate in topological order. If both predecessor wires already have constant replacements, the gate output is constant and requires no gate. If one predecessor is constant and the other is a wire carrying a restricted function, the gate's induced unary map is one of the four unary Boolean maps: constant 0, constant 1, identity, or negation. The first three require no gate (constant wires may be supplied freely; identity is the existing wire). Negation is implemented by one allowed binary gate with both inputs tied to the existing wire, for example NAND(z,z). If neither predecessor is constant, retain the original binary gate. Thus each original gate is replaced by zero or one gate, and no original gate creates more than one replacement gate. Reusing a replacement wire wherever the original gate output was used preserves unrestricted fan-out. The resulting circuit computes exactly the restriction and has at most s gates.
scope: All m>=1, all fan-in-two DAG circuits with gates from the full set of 16 Boolean binary operations, free input/constants, unrestricted fan-out; restriction fixes one input to either Boolean value.
limitation: The bound is non-increasing only. It gives no strict gate decrease, since a gate may become a negation and still cost one gate. It therefore does not imply the MCSP[m^c] circuit lower bound or close the superlinear accumulation gap.

label: S0358
statement: statement: For every m>=1, s>=0, Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} computable by a fan-in-two DAG circuit with at most s gates from all 16 binary Boolean operations and free input wires has each coordinate cofactor f_{i=b} computable in the same model with at most s gates. Proof: Traverse the circuit in topological order, replacing x_i by b. Represent each wire by a constant, a free input, or a retained gate output. For each gate, substitute its predecessor representatives. If the resulting operation is constant or a projection, use that constant or predecessor wire and omit the gate; otherwise retain one gate for the induced binary Boolean operation, which is among the 16 allowed operations. Reuse representatives at every fan-out occurrence. By induction, each representative computes the restricted value of its original wire, so the output computes f_{i=b}; at most one gate is retained per original gate. Therefore MCSP[s] YES instances remain YES under coordinate cofactors. This gives no lower bound on the number of gates omitted or on the MCSP decision circuit.

label: S0359
statement: For every m>=1 and integer s>=0, the language MCSP_m[s] on truth tables y in {0,1}^{2^m}, with yes iff y is computed by a fan-in-two circuit of at most s gates over all 16 binary Boolean operations, has a nondeterministic verifier whose witness length is at most 1+ceil(log2(s+1))+s(4+2ceil(log2(m+s+1))) bits and whose running time is O(2^m(m+s)+s log(m+s)). Proof: A witness gives j<=s, then for each gate i in topological order its operation (4 bits) and its two predecessor wire indices, each in {1,...,m+i-1}, using ceil(log2(m+s+1)) bits per index, and finally an output wire index among {1,...,m+s}, also using at most ceil(log2(m+s+1)) bits. The verifier rejects malformed encodings or indices that do not refer to inputs or earlier gates. It evaluates the described circuit on each of the 2^m inputs, comparing the result bit with the corresponding truth-table bit, and accepts iff every comparison agrees. If y is in MCSP_m[s], a topological listing of a witnessing circuit supplies such a witness and it passes. If the verifier accepts, the checked circuit has at most s gates and agrees with y on every input, so y is in MCSP_m[s]. The encoding and evaluation bounds follow directly. In particular, for fixed c>=1 and s=floor(m^c), the witness length is O(m^c log m) and verification time is 2^m poly(m). This is a characterization of the decision problem's NP witness, not a lower bound on its deterministic circuit size.

label: S0360
statement: statement: For m>=2 and any integer s>=0, let D_m[s] be the Boolean function on 2^m truth-table bits that accepts exactly tables of m-input functions of fan-in-two circuit complexity at most s, where the basis contains all 16 binary Boolean operations and input wires are free. Let E_m map a 2^(m-1)-bit table y, indexed by z in {0,1}^{m-1}, to the 2^m-bit table E_m(y) with E_m(y)_(0,z)=E_m(y)_(1,z)=y_z. Then D_{m-1}[s](y)=D_m[s](E_m(y)) for every y. Consequently any Boolean circuit of size S computing D_m[s] yields one of size at most S computing D_{m-1}[s]. Proof: E_m(y) is the truth table of f(x_1,z)=g(z), where g has table y. A circuit for g computes f without using x_1, so C_m(f)<=C_{m-1}(g). Conversely, restricting x_1 to 0 in any circuit for f gives a circuit for g with no more gates: each gate is retained with its predecessor wires substituted, and constant wires arising from the fixed input may be propagated without adding gates. Thus C_{m-1}(g)<=C_m(f), so the complexities are equal and the decision identity follows. Substituting the duplicated input wires into a size-S circuit for D_m[s] computes the composed decision function without increasing its gate count. This exact restriction relation transfers upper bounds on MCSP decision-circuit size from dimension m to dimension m-1; it supplies no lower bound and does not close the target obligation.

label: S0361
statement: Let m>=1, c>=1 be fixed, N=2^m, g=floor(m^c), and A the set of m-input Boolean functions computable by at most g fan-in-two gates over all 16 binary Boolean operations. For every fixed 0<=delta<1/2, the fraction of truth tables at Hamming distance at most floor(delta N) from A is at most (g+1)(m+g+1)[16(m+g+1)^2]^g * 2^(N H_2(delta)) / 2^N, and hence tends to zero as m tends to infinity. Proof: For j gates, encode the ordered operation and two predecessor wires of each gate in topological order and then the output wire. Summing over 0<=j<=g gives |A| <= (g+1)(m+g+1)[16(m+g+1)^2]^g. For each a in A the Hamming ball of radius floor(delta N) contains at most sum_{i<=delta N} binom(N,i) <= 2^(N H_2(delta)) tables. The union bound gives the fraction stated. Its base-2 logarithm is O(m^c log m)-N(1-H_2(delta)), which tends to minus infinity for fixed c and delta<1/2.

label: S0362
statement:
statement_start: For every m>=1 and every Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, if f_0,f_1 are its cofactors on the last input and C denotes minimum fan-in-two DAG gate count over all 16 binary Boolean operations with free input wires, then C(f) <= C(f_0)+C(f_1)+3.
statement: For every m>=1 and every Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, let f_b(x_1,...,x_{m-1})=f(x_1,...,x_{m-1},b) for b in {0,1}. In the fan-in-two Boolean DAG circuit model over all 16 binary Boolean operations, with free input wires, the minimum gate count satisfies C_m(f) <= C_{m-1}(f_0)+C_{m-1}(f_1)+3. Proof: Take minimum circuits for f_0 and f_1 on the first m-1 input wires and combine their outputs u=f_0(x_1,...,x_{m-1}) and v=f_1(x_1,...,x_{m-1}). Add three fan-in-two gates: d=u XOR v, e=x_m AND d, and output u XOR e. If x_m=0 the output is u; if x_m=1 it is u XOR (u XOR v)=v. Thus it computes f and uses exactly three additional gates. The two cofactor circuits may be placed side by side in a DAG, so total size is at most their sum plus three. This holds also for m=1, where the cofactors are constants/free wires (or constants computed with at most one gate if the model has no constant wires), with the stated bound still valid.

label: S0363
statement: Let c>=1 be fixed, m>=1, N=2^m, g=floor(m^c), and let A_m be the set of truth tables computed by fan-in-two circuits with at most g gates over the 16 binary Boolean operations. Let delta_m be any sequence in [0,1/2). The fraction of N-bit truth tables at Hamming distance at most floor(delta_m N) from A_m is at most min(1, B_m 2^{-N(1-H_2(delta_m))}), where B_m=(g+1)(m+g+1)[16(m+g+1)^2]^g and H_2(u)=-u log_2(u)-(1-u)log_2(1-u), with endpoint values by continuity. In particular, if N(1-H_2(delta_m))-log_2(B_m) tends to +infinity, this neighborhood fraction tends to zero. Proof: For j<=g, encode a circuit by its ordered gate operations, predecessor wires and output wire. The number of such descriptions summed over j is at most B_m, so |A_m|<=B_m. For each a in A_m its radius-r Hamming ball has sum_{i=0}^r binom(N,i) points, where r=floor(delta_m N). Since delta_m<1/2, the binomial sum is at most 2^{N H_2(delta_m)}. The union bound gives at most B_m 2^{N H_2(delta_m)} points in the union; divide by 2^N and cap at 1. The final implication is immediate by taking base-2 logarithms. This is a sparsity statement about neighborhoods of easy truth tables; it does not bound the circuit size of the MCSP decision function.

label: S0365
statement:
statement_start: For every m>=k>=0 and every Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, if each of its 2^k cofactors obtained by fixing the first k input variables has fan-in-two DAG circuit complexity at most t over all 16 binary Boolean gates with free input and constant wires, then C_m(f) <= 2^k t + 3(2^k-1).
statement: For every m>=k>=0 and every Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, if each of its 2^k cofactors obtained by fixing the first k input variables has fan-in-two DAG circuit complexity at most t over all 16 binary Boolean gates with free input and constant wires, then C_m(f) <= 2^k t + 3(2^k-1). Proof: Arrange the 2^k cofactors as leaves of the complete binary decision tree on x_1,...,x_k. At each internal node, let u and v be the outputs of the already constructed circuits for its two child cofactors, corresponding to the next variable x_i=0 and x_i=1. Construct the parent output as u XOR (x_i AND (u XOR v)), using three fan-in-two gates. This equals u when x_i=0 and v when x_i=1. Starting with 2^k leaf circuits, the tree has exactly 2^k-1 internal nodes, so the total number of gates is at most 2^k t+3(2^k-1); sharing among subcircuits could only reduce it. This is a constructive upper bound for individual function complexity. It does not imply a lower bound on the MCSP decision function and does not close G0001 or G0002.

label: S0366
statement: statement: For every fan-in-two Boolean circuit C and every partial assignment rho to its input variables, the cofactor C|rho has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of size at most |C| in the same gate basis. Proof: Replace each input fixed by rho with its constant value. Process gates in topological order. Whenever the resulting gate has constant output, replace it by that constant; otherwise retain one gate with its original two predecessor wires, which are either constants, free remaining input wires, or outputs of retained earlier gates. Induction on the topological order shows every retained wire has the same value as its source gate under the fixed assignment, for every assignment to the unfixed inputs. The output therefore computes C|rho, and no new gate was introduced, so its size is at most |C|.
